source.title: Beyond adaptive gradient: Fast-Controlled Minibatch Algorithm for large-scale optimization
source.authors: Corrado Coppola; Lorenzo Papa; Irene Amerini; L. Palagi

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares optimizer choices on image classification and reports validation accuracy, a different measure of optimizer generalization performance than the version's stated training-to-test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-accuracy comparisons for multiple optimizers. Training accuracy and train-to-test gaps are not reported. Theoretical convergence claims and cited optimizer findings are not experimental results for this claim.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy using ImageNet-initialized networks and mostly default hyperparameters. This tests V4 in a transfer-learning setting; V4 does not require a measured training-to-test gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors claim F-CMA usually achieves higher validation accuracy faster, reducing training time, and describe their experiments as validating its theoretical convergence properties.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares optimizers using default hyperparameters, with SGD's learning rate reduced from its original setting because it did not converge; it does not report training accuracy or train-to-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Model architecture and dataset; the reported validation accuracies vary across optimizer-model-dataset combinations.
record.problems: The reported metric is validation accuracy, not the training-to-test gap; the paper gives no uncertainty estimates and does not report training accuracy. Optimizer settings are mostly defaults, with SGD's learning rate changed.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 includes many additional model-optimizer-dataset combinations. They are omitted because the 60-row limit prioritizes representative direct Adam-versus-SGD comparisons; no values were aggregated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Equal or better training performance; learning-rate and schedule tuning searches; broader tuning; controlled recovery through decoupled weight decay or optimizer switching; language benchmarks. AdamW is included, but its comparison does not isolate weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that recover large-batch accuracy.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and comparing against random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The two recorded comparisons cannot support a Swin-B verdict. Table 2 contains mixed Adam-versus-SGD outcomes, including lower Adam accuracy on both actual Swin-B tasks. Other comparisons are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing or assigned verdicts without linked rows. The reported comparisons lack uncertainty estimates, and mostly default settings do not establish performance after systematic tuning. F-CMA's own performance advantage and stationary-point convergence proof do not independently test these claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Training-performance comparisons, language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed-epoch generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-initialized ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, batch size 128, 250 epochs, default Adam settings and SGD learning rate 0.01
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show Adam exceeding SGD by 2.40 and 0.48 percentage points, respectively; these conditions reverse the adaptive-optimizer disadvantage.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded SGD's accuracy on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, but these comparisons remain unverified.
